meta.inspiration: A manager's year in a company with a problem: four quarters, a team, hidden facts that sponsors state wrongly, one market event and a plan for the year after.
meta.rights_note: Original scenario. The company, the people, the product and every number are invented.

company.name: Brightkart
company.one_liner: A checkout and order service used by about 3,500 online stores in India, nine engineers, and a festival sale two quarters away.
company.market: India: online stores of every size, with sharp spikes at festival sales
company.business_model: A fee on every order that goes through checkout, with higher tiers for large merchants.
company.product: The checkout and order service, and the API merchants build against.
company.role: Tech lead for checkout and orders. Your team is nine engineers, one designer and two analysts.
company.brief: You report to the CTO. The platform has grown by shortcuts, and the festival sale in two quarters will show whether it holds. Product wants new features, the architect wants a rewrite, and nobody can say where checkout time really goes, because production has almost no tracing. You have four quarters of twelve weeks.

stakeholders.name: Preeti Chandra
stakeholders.says: I will back the plan that keeps checkout up on sale day. Tell me what you know, not what you fear.

stakeholders.name: Nikhil Arora
stakeholders.says: Merchants keep asking for bulk exports and a self-serve API. Every quarter we say no, we lose deals.

stakeholders.name: Sanjay Kulkarni
stakeholders.says: The order service is beyond saving. A rewrite is the only honest answer, and the design documents show it is a clean job.

stakeholders.name: Ritu Malhotra
stakeholders.says: Our scan says the payments library is fine. We have not had a finding in a year.

stakeholders.name: Dev Menon
stakeholders.says: On-call is burning people out. It is the database, I am sure of it, but I cannot show you, because we have no traces in production.

stakeholders.name: Karan Shah
stakeholders.says: A self-serve API will triple small-store sign-ups. Every developer I meet at events can do it in an afternoon.

segments.name: Small online stores
segments.description: Stores of one to ten people on a hosted shop builder.

segments.name: Mid-size retailers
segments.description: Brands and retailers with their own engineers.

segments.name: Marketplaces and large brands
segments.description: A few dozen merchants who bring most of the volume.

items.name: Move order writes to a queue
items.about: Take order writes off the checkout path so a burst cannot lock the table.

items.name: Make payment retries safe
items.about: Idempotency keys, so a retried payment can never charge twice.

items.name: Timeouts and circuit breakers
items.about: Fail fast and shed load when a dependency is slow, instead of queueing everything behind it.

items.name: Fix the flaky test suite
items.about: Quarantine and repair the tests nobody trusts, so a green build means something.

items.name: Tracing and dashboards in production
items.about: Trace every checkout end to end, so the team can see where the time goes. Raises measurement to level 2.

items.name: Feature flags and safe rollouts
items.about: Ship behind flags and roll back in seconds.

items.name: Upgrade the payments library past end of support
items.about: Replace the library the vendor stopped patching.

items.name: Shard the orders database
items.about: Split orders across databases so one hot merchant cannot lock everyone.

items.name: Rewrite the order service
items.about: Rebuild the order service cleanly beside the old one and cut over. The principal engineer's favourite.

items.name: Self-serve onboarding API
items.about: Let a store integrate without talking to anyone: keys, a sandbox, docs and a checklist.

items.name: Bulk order export for large merchants
items.about: Scheduled exports of every order, in the formats finance teams ask for.

items.name: Checkout latency sprint
items.about: Profile and trim the slowest steps in checkout.

items.name: Reliable webhooks
items.about: Retries, ordering and a replay tool for the events merchants depend on.

items.name: Developer sandbox and docs
items.about: A sandbox that behaves like production, and documentation written for the people who read it.

hidden.label: Share of checkout slowdowns caused by database locks
hidden.description: The site reliability lead blames the database. The traces that would show it were never switched on in production.

hidden.label: How tangled the order service really is, against what the rewrite plan assumes
hidden.description: The principal engineer scoped the rewrite from the design documents. Nobody has read the code the documents describe.

hidden.label: Share of small stores that will integrate without help
hidden.description: Sales assumes the developers they meet at events are typical of small stores.

hidden.label: How exposed the old payments library really is
hidden.description: The security scan was run against staging, which is not configured like production.

events.name: Checkout falls over on sale day
events.signal: Checkout is timing out during the festival sale, and orders are queueing behind each other in the database.
events.body: A burst of sale-day traffic locks the orders table. Merchants lose sales in the busiest hours of the year and blame the platform.

directions.label: Shed load, queue orders and tell merchants plainly

events.name: A critical flaw in the payments library
events.signal: A researcher has published a critical flaw in the payments library you depend on, and two large merchants want your answer by Friday.
events.body: The flaw is real and reachable in production. Until it is patched, large merchants may pause processing.

causes.label: A rival is stirring it up

directions.label: Patch, disclose and tell merchants plainly
Say it does not affect us

events.name: The strongest engineer gives notice
events.signal: Your strongest engineer has given notice, and on-call has been exhausting for a month.
events.body: Burnout, not money. The person who knows the order service best leaves in four weeks.

directions.label: Fix on-call, pair up and write down what they know

plans.name: Modernise in steps
plans.pitch: Keep shipping while paying the platform down a quarter at a time.

plans.name: Rewrite the core
plans.pitch: Stop the line and rebuild the order service properly.

plans.name: Hold and ship
plans.pitch: Leave the platform as it is and give the business every feature it asks for.

root.prompt: Which of these do you believe is behind the slow, fragile checkout?

measurement.label: Logs and alerts
measurement.shows: Arrivals, orders processed, merchants and the money. Nothing in between.

measurement.label: Core events
measurement.shows: Also the first step and the share of customers lost each quarter.

measurement.label: The full funnel
measurement.shows: Also every step and every conversion rate, by segment.

quarters.title: The sale is coming
quarters.opening: {company} makes {hold_profit} a quarter and has {cash} in the bank. The festival sale is two quarters away. Of every 100 small stores that start, {per100_small} end up processing orders. Your team has about {road} weeks of engineering this quarter, and every one of them is spoken for.

quarters.title: First results
quarters.opening: Last quarter {shipped} shipped. Profit was {profit}, {delta} on the quarter before. {learned} {pleased}

quarters.title: The shock
quarters.opening: Last quarter {shipped} shipped and profit was {profit}. Something has changed outside the team. Read the signal below, say what you think is behind it and whether you checked, and decide how to answer.

quarters.title: The term sheet
quarters.opening: The board will back one of three plans for next year. Profit last quarter was {profit}. Where you stand: usability {U}, reliability {R}, technical debt {D}, engineering trust {trust_eng}, leadership trust {trust_lead}.
